documents.title: UTDSP5017 Generative AI Use in Academic Work
documents.summary: University policy issued 2025-03-24 that gives faculty the discretion to permit, partly allow or prohibit generative AI and requires them to say so before work begins and in syllabi and assignments. It sets student duties for each case (cite and verify when permitted, follow written guidelines for partial use, no AI when prohibited) and ties misuse to the Student Code of Conduct.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no default itself: "Faculty have the discretion to permit, prohibit, or partially allow the use of generative AI" and "Faculty have the freedom and responsibility to determine how generative AI can be used". It names three cases (permitted, partial, prohibited), so the stance is delegates with those tiers.

Source: "Consult OIT: For personalized guidance on selecting and utilizing AI tools and Models effectively". The service helps any user choose tools; it does not send students to human help in place of AI, so the stretched fit is rejected and UNCOVERED kept. A's fit note is merged into the uncovered note.

units.why: "Report AI/Gen AI Issue: To report any issues related to AI/Gen AI tools across campus to OIT" gives a channel for reporting AI problems (P71).
units.anchor: To report any issues related to AI/Gen AI tools across campus to OIT.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, phase, modality and type. Codes follow the shared reading of the source.

notes: Coded only the two included university-layer documents. Recurring UNCOVERED pattern: a bare expectation of ethical, responsible, transparent AI use (one unit in each document). Atlas page: example tables (students/faculty/departments uses) were skipped as illustrations, not rules. Course layer deferred in the collect file; no school or computing policy found. Atlas document stance resolved to encourage (coder B had permit).
